newsitem.title: UK: Railtrack says H1 results show progress.
newsitem.headline: Railtrack says H1 results show progress.

text.p: British railways owner Railtrack Plc on Friday announced a 12 percent rise in operating profits in the first results since its privatisation in May, and vowed to create the world's best railway.

Headline pretax profits for the six months to September 30 jumped to 173 million pounds ($288 million) from 98 million pounds a year ago, boosted by a drop in interest charges of 43 million pounds because the government cut its debt burden before privatisation.
Operating profits rose to 169 million pounds from 151 million a year earlier and the company declared its first dividend of 7.3 pence a share.

"This has been a landmark half-year for Railtrack. The success of our flotation in May has been accompanied by real progress in the renaissaance of the railways," chairman Robert Horton said in his results statement.
"We will continue to give high priority to maintaining our close relationship with the rail regulator to deliver the world's most safe, reliable and efficient commercial railway," he said.
The prospectus for Railtrack's selloff had said it would have paid an interim dividend of 6.85 pence a year ago and analysts expected to see between 7.3 and 7.45 pence this time.
Earnings were up four percent at 29 pence a share against a proforma figure of 27.8 pence a year ago.

Railtrack finance director Norman Broadhurst told reporters in a telephone news conference that the company has promised "a progressive dividend policy" and earnings cover would be addressed "once we have a track record."
